speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your left knee over the past two months. To help me understand your condition better, how would you describe the nature of this pain, and did it start after any specific injury or event?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the fact that the pain is severe enough to wake you from sleep and hasn't responded to ibuprofen suggests an inflammatory or structural issue rather than simple strain. Given your age and the chronicity of the swelling, have you noticed any joint effusion (fluid buildup), stiffness, or warmth when you touch the knee? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, and Rheumatoid Factor.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of the Bone. The clinical presentation of night pain and swelling in a young adult, combined with the specific radiographic finding of a lytic lesion with a "soap bubble" appearance in the distal femur, is highly characteristic of this condition. The normal inflammatory markers and lack of response to NSAIDs further support a primary bone neoplasm rather than an infectious or inflammatory process.
